name: 10-25976-d6ts-a051
notes: South Shore Watershed Association (SSWA) annually monitors main tributaries in each of its five constituent watersheds: DeSable River, Westmoreland River, Tryon River, Augustine Cove-Cape Traverse and Seven Mile Bay, to determine the health of our rivers and the effects that stream restoration techniques have on enhancing future river health. SSWA will also be continuing its partnership with Bedeque Bay Environmental Management Association (BBEMA) to track water quality parameters. Only by tracking the changes in our water conditions can SSWA accurately determine which of our stream restoration techniques will have a lasting effect on the watershed habitat.

notes_translated.en: South Shore Watershed Association (SSWA) annually monitors main tributaries in each of its five constituent watersheds: DeSable River, Westmoreland River, Tryon River, Augustine Cove-Cape Traverse and Seven Mile Bay, to determine the health of our rivers and the effects that stream restoration techniques have on enhancing future river health. SSWA will also be continuing its partnership with Bedeque Bay Environmental Management Association (BBEMA) to track water quality parameters. Only by tracking the changes in our water conditions can SSWA accurately determine which of our stream restoration techniques will have a lasting effect on the watershed habitat.
notes_translated.fr: La South Shore Watershed Association (SSWA) surveille chaque année les principaux affluents de chacun de ses cinq bassins versants constitutifs : la rivière DeSable, la rivière Westmoreland, la rivière Tryon, Augustine Cove-Cape Traverse et la baie Seven Mile, afin de déterminer l'état de santé de nos rivières et les effets des techniques de restauration des cours d'eau sur l'amélioration de la santé future des rivières. La SSWA poursuivra également son partenariat avec la Bedeque Bay Environmental Management Association (BBEMA) pour suivre les paramètres de qualité de l'eau. Ce n'est qu'en suivant l'évolution de nos conditions d'eau que la SSWA peut déterminer avec précision laquelle de nos techniques de restauration des cours d'eau aura un effet durable sur l'habitat du bassin versant.
